stem: A company runs an order system in which Amazon EC2 instances process messages from an Amazon SQS queue. On some nights the consumers stop working for a while, and customers notice late orders the next morning. The operations team wants to monitor the queue and receive an alarm when messages wait too long before a consumer processes them. Which Amazon CloudWatch metric should the alarm use?
keywords: messages wait too long before a consumer processes them

options.text: The ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible metric of the queue
options.why: It counts messages [received but not yet deleted or expired](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-metric-not-visible-messages-is-in-flight), so it shows work in progress, and stopped consumers receive nothing.

options.text: The NumberOfMessagesSent metric of the queue
options.why: It counts the messages that producers add to the queue, so it shows arrivals, not how long any message waits.
options.misconception: The number of arriving messages shows how long messages wait.

options.text: The ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric of the queue
options.why: It reports the age of the [oldest unprocessed message in the queue](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-metric-age-of-oldest-message-measures-lag), which is the wait that the team wants to watch.

options.text: The CPUUtilization metric of the consumer instances
options.why: CPU shows how busy the instances are; stopped consumers use little CPU, so the alarm stays quiet when orders wait.
options.misconception: Instance CPU shows how long messages wait in a queue.

explanation: The team cares about how long messages wait, not how many arrive. [ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-metric-age-of-oldest-message-measures-lag) reports the age of the oldest unprocessed message. When the consumers stop, that age grows, so an alarm on it fires whatever the number of instances.
takeaway: To alarm on waiting time, watch ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage; to scale workers, use the backlog per instance.
twin: If the stem said "scale the consumers so that the backlog stays small" instead: the [backlog per instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-sqs-backlog-per-instance), because a target tracking policy needs a value that moves with the group size.
say: Wait time is the age of the oldest message, so I'd alarm on ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage.
